## Specification
`/Users/boo/Github/project/astertable/kickoff/tablekeeper/spec/stage-2.md` — the stage-1 spec
(`.../stage-1.md`) continues to apply. Paste the COMPLETE text of both files into every delegated
handoff; a path or room reference alone is insufficient. Do not implement stages 3 or 4.

## Stage folder rules
- Copy `stage-1/` to `stage-2/` and extend the copy. Leave `stage-1/` unchanged and still passing.
- `stage-2/` must be a complete service: source, `Dockerfile`, `RUN.md` (one command builds and
starts it). No nested `.git`, no symlinks.
- Keep AsterTable's stack: Go + chi + pgx + PostgreSQL 18 embedded in the single image. Add the
browser UI with React 19 + TypeScript + Vite, built during `docker build` and served by the
same container on the same `PORT`. All assets (fonts, scripts, styles, icons) local; no CDN or
runtime network.

## Product direction from the product owner (in addition to the spec)
- Show the diner where their booking is with a **booking status rail**: a short, animated sequence
next to the booking form, e.g. *Table selected → Sending to the restaurant → Confirmed*.
- The rail must be driven **only by the real request state**, never by timers or invented steps:
- *Sending* is shown while the booking request is in flight;
- *Confirmed* appears only after the server's successful response, with the original reference;
- a lost or failed-to-arrive response moves the rail to an *uncertain* step that explains the same
request is being retried with the same idempotency key and body (this is the `booking-uncertain`
state);
- a `409 table_unavailable` moves it to a *refused* step, refreshes availability and keeps the form
(this is the `booking-error` state).
- Each step must be distinguishable without colour alone (icon + text), announced to assistive
technology (e.g. a polite live region), and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Never show raw browser or server error text to the diner (e.g. "Failed to fetch", "Load failed”,
"NetworkError", or technical server messages). Translate every failure into a short, friendly
sentence that says what happened and what to do next, specific to the screen (search, sign-in,
booking, lookup, cancel). A booking whose response is lost still follows the uncertain/retry rule.
- The rail is presentation only. It must not change any required `data-testid`, required text rule,
or the retry semantics in the spec.

## Working rules
- Literal `@handle` addressing in both directions for assignments, questions, rejections, repairs.
- Implementer writes and commits production code and tests. Conformance Reviewer independently
checks the exact commit against the full spec and writes no production code. Adversarial
Verifier runs black-box, browser, concurrency and clean-environment campaigns and writes test
tooling only. Coordinator writes no production code and accepts no self-review.
- Build to the specification, not to the shipped checks; the shipped Stage 2 checks are a small
fraction of the graded suite.
- Gate every candidate with the official harness into a NEW output directory and require
`claimed stage: 2` with Stage 1 still passing; finish with isolated mode:
`cd /Users/boo/Github/project/astertable/kickoff && ./.venv/bin/python -m harness run --track tablekeeper --repo ../band-work/result --stage 2 --mode isolated --out ../band-work/checks/final-s2-<purpose>-<date>-<n>`
- Preserve all commits; never amend, rebase or squash another seat's history.

## Verification focus (from the spec; not an exhaustive list)
- Browser flows at 375 px and desktop width with no horizontal scroll; visible labels and focus;
distinct available / unavailable / selected / loading / success / refused / uncertain states.
- Every required `data-testid`, exact text rules (`confirmation-reference`, `reservation-status`),
and `data-available` correctness against `GET /availability` for the searched party size.
- Out-of-order searches show only the latest search; `409 table_unavailable` shows `booking-error`,
refreshes availability and keeps the form; a lost response shows `booking-uncertain` and the
unchanged form retries with the same idempotency key and body until the original reference shows.
- Resubmitting the unchanged form returns the same reference; changing a field makes a new request.
- Combined tables: `combinable` pairs only, non-transitive; `available_options` ordering;
`table_ids` vs `table_id` rules and errors; both tables occupied for the full duration; pairs in
PATCH, cancel and reservation moves; combination cells and labels in the UI.
- Upgrade: a Stage 1 export imports into Stage 2; a signed-in browser stays signed in; a lost
booking before export is still retryable after import and recovers the original confirmation.
- Concurrent bookings and amendments linearizable; no 5xx under any input or load.

## Done means
`stage-2/` independently reviewed and adversarially verified, isolated harness `claimed stage: 2`
with Stage 1 green, rejections repaired and re-verified. Final report: commits, commands and
results, rejection/repair evidence, elapsed time, model usage/cost if available, residual risks,
and the exact next step.

S1-LIMITS, S1-RUNTIME, S1-BROWSE, S1-DATA, S1-OCC, S1-HTTP, S1-CLEAN, S1-HARNESS, with regression protection for S1-SCOPE through S1-MOVES and repaired S1-EXIM semantics.

Design summary and measured bottleneck:
The cold-date local-time resolver scanned a 76-hour UTC window one second at a time (273,600 iterations per date) while holding one global mutex. Fifty distinct cold availability dates therefore serialized before reaching the normal availability path. The repair derives every offset in force from Go's loaded IANA ZoneBounds, round-trips all 1,440 local minutes through those offsets, sorts fold matches by instant so the first occurrence remains authoritative, computes cache misses outside the write lock, and uses read locking for immutable hits. The 128-date cache cap remains. Availability SQL, occupancy checks, mutation paths, and linearizability semantics are unchanged.

# Dark Factory — WeAreDevelopers hackathon

This is the kickoff package for the [WeAreDevelopers hackathon on lablab.ai](https://lablab.ai/ai-hackathons/wearedevelopers-hackathon).
You build a software factory in Band Desktop — at least three coding-agent seats that
plan, implement and review each other's work — and have it build a service, one stage at
a time.

**Read the [participant guide](docs/participant-guide.md) before anything else.** It is
the authoritative source for the rules, schedule, gates, rubric and submission steps.
This README only tells you where things are.

## What's in this repository

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`docs/participant-guide.md`](docs/participant-guide.md) | Rules, schedule, rubric and step-by-step instructions |
| `tablekeeper/` | Track 1: a restaurant reservation system. `spec/stage-1.md`…`stage-4.md` and part of each stage's tests |
| `pocketful/` | Track 2: a wallet and payments app. Same layout as `tablekeeper/` |
| `toy/` | Unscored practice track: a shared counter, with its full test suite and sample mandates |
| `scaffold/` | Minimal Python starting service, used only by the toy walkthrough |
| `harness/` | The `python -m harness` CLI that builds your stage folders and runs the checks |

Pick one track and stay in it. The result you submit is a **separate** repository your
band builds; nothing you submit goes into this one.

## Help

- Band Desktop, seats, permissions and the harness: the
  [BAND Discord](https://discord.com/invite/5YkNXmYfjk).
- Registration, uploads and prizes: the lablab Discord channel.
- Spec ambiguities: ask in the BAND Discord. Answers are shared publicly with every team.
